html:
The Old Kingdom was the first great age of Egyptian civilisation, from about 2686 to 2181 BCE, when kings ruling from Memphis built the pyramids. It covers the Third to Sixth Dynasties. Dates differ by a few decades between scholars.

It began with stone. Around 2650 BCE King Djoser and his official Imhotep built the Step Pyramid at Saqqara, the first large building made all of cut stone. The kings who followed learned fast:

  • Sneferu built three pyramids and reached the first true smooth-sided pyramid.
  • His son Khufu built the Great Pyramid of Giza, the largest ever built.
  • Khafre and Menkaure built the other two pyramids at Giza, and the Great Sphinx is usually linked to Khafre.

Building on this scale needed a strong state. The king was a god who held the land in order, and an army of scribes counted harvests, organised labour and ran the stone quarries. Expeditions went to Sinai for copper and turquoise and south into Nubia.

Later kings built smaller pyramids, and from King Unas onward their burial chambers were carved with the Pyramid Texts, the oldest religious writings in Egypt. Power slowly shifted to governors in the provinces. After the very long reign of Pepi II, and a time of low Nile floods, the central state broke apart into the First Intermediate Period. Egypt was reunited about a century later in the Middle Kingdom.
sum: The Old Kingdom was the first great age of Egyptian civilisation, from about 2686 to 2181 BCE, when kings ruling from Memphis built the pyramids. It covers the Third to Sixth Dynasties. Dates differ by a few decades between scholars.
